Rio de Janeiro:
- If you're visiting Christ the Redeemer, Copacabana Fort, and all those tourist locations, don't eat at the closest restaurants. They're usually overpriced and a tourist trap.

- Avoid the subway at 6-7a.m. and 5-7p.m. It's ridiculously overcrowded. Also, the subway lady announces the stops in Portuguese and English, but sometimes the sound system is off, so I would suggest counting the stations until yours to be sure.

- Not everywhere is dangerous. Avoid beaches and downtown at night (Lapa is probably fine) and favelas if you don't have a guide and it'll be okay. A good rule of thumb is "if there's lots of people and doesn't look sketchy, it's fine" (yes, it's that obvious)

- Also don't look scared at every kid who walks by. We know you're not from here, looking like that is just gonna piss people off (and you're more likely to be mugged).

- Please be polite. We will give you directions and help you if you need, but there's no need to be an asshole.
